Decide whether a tic-tac-toe board is a win, a draw or a game still going, or explain why no game played by the rules could have left it.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/state-of-tic-tac-toe) (MIT). Listed under [Games & Simulation](/examples/?subject=games-and-simulation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: state_of_tic_tac_toe.nomi
//# Where a game of tic-tac-toe stands, and whether its board is valid.

/// Where a valid game stands.
pub enum State {
    Win
    Draw
    Ongoing
}

/// Why a board cannot come from a game played by the rules.
pub enum Error {
    XWentTwice
    OStarted
    PlayedAfterWin
}

impl Display for Error {
    fn to_string(error: Error) -> String {
        case error {
            .XWentTwice -> "Wrong turn order: X went twice"
            .OStarted -> "Wrong turn order: O started"
            .PlayedAfterWin -> "Impossible board: game should have ended after the game was won"
        }
    }
}

/// The positions of the eight lines that win, in a board read row by row:
/// three rows, three columns and two diagonals.
once lines = [
    #[0, 1, 2],
    #[3, 4, 5],
    #[6, 7, 8],
    #[0, 3, 6],
    #[1, 4, 7],
    #[2, 5, 8],
    #[0, 4, 8],
    #[2, 4, 6],
]

/// The state of the game on `board`, three rows of three cells, each `X`,
/// `O` or a space. X plays first, and the game stops at the first line of
/// three.
pub fn gamestate(board: List<String>) -> Result<State, Error> {
    cells =
        board
        |> Iter.flat_map(String.to_codepoints)
        |> Iter.to_vector()

    xs = marks(cells, 'X')
    os = marks(cells, 'O')
    x_won = has_won(cells, 'X')
    o_won = has_won(cells, 'O')

    case {
        os > xs -> Err(.OStarted)
        xs > os + 1 -> Err(.XWentTwice)
        x_won and (o_won or xs == os) or o_won and xs > os -> Err(.PlayedAfterWin)
        x_won or o_won -> Ok(.Win)
        xs + os == 9 -> Ok(.Draw)
        _ -> Ok(.Ongoing)
    }
}

/// How many cells hold `mark`.
fn marks(cells: Vector<Codepoint>, mark: Codepoint) -> Int {
    cells
    |> Iter.filter(&(&1 == mark))
    |> Iter.count()
}

/// Whether `mark` fills one of the lines.
fn has_won(cells: Vector<Codepoint>, mark: Codepoint) -> Bool {
    Iter.any(lines, fn line -> Iter.all(line, &(Vector.get(cells, &1)! == mark)))
}

// FILE: state_of_tic_tac_toe_test.nomi
import state_of_tic_tac_toe.{self, State}

test "won games" {
    cases = [
        #("Finished game where X won via left column victory", ["XOO", "X  ", "X  "]),
        #("Finished game where X won via middle column victory", ["OXO", " X ", " X "]),
        #("Finished game where X won via right column victory", ["OOX", "  X", "  X"]),
        #("Finished game where O won via left column victory", ["OXX", "OX ", "O  "]),
        #("Finished game where O won via middle column victory", ["XOX", " OX", " O "]),
        #("Finished game where O won via right column victory", ["XXO", " XO", "  O"]),
        #("Finished game where X won via top row victory", ["XXX", "XOO", "O  "]),
        #("Finished game where X won via middle row victory", ["O  ", "XXX", " O "]),
        #("Finished game where X won via bottom row victory", [" OO", "O X", "XXX"]),
        #("Finished game where O won via top row victory", ["OOO", "XXO", "XX "]),
        #("Finished game where O won via middle row victory", ["XX ", "OOO", "X  "]),
        #("Finished game where O won via bottom row victory", ["XOX", " XX", "OOO"]),
        #("Finished game where X won via falling diagonal victory", ["XOO", " X ", "  X"]),
        #("Finished game where X won via rising diagonal victory", ["O X", "OX ", "X  "]),
        #("Finished game where O won via falling diagonal victory", ["OXX", "OOX", "X O"]),
        #("Finished game where O won via rising diagonal victory", ["  O", " OX", "OXX"]),
        #("Finished game where X won via a row and a column victory", ["XXX", "XOO", "XOO"]),
        #("Finished game where X won via two diagonal victories", ["XOX", "OXO", "XOX"]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, board), description {
        assert state_of_tic_tac_toe.gamestate(board) == Ok(State.Win)
    }
}

test "drawn games" {
    cases = [
        #("Draw", ["XOX", "XXO", "OXO"]),
        #("Another draw", ["XXO", "OXX", "XOO"]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, board), description {
        assert state_of_tic_tac_toe.gamestate(board) == Ok(State.Draw)
    }
}

test "ongoing games" {
    cases = [
        #("Ongoing game: one move in", ["   ", "X  ", "   "]),
        #("Ongoing game: two moves in", ["O  ", " X ", "   "]),
        #("Ongoing game: five moves in", ["X  ", " XO", "OX "]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, board), description {
        assert state_of_tic_tac_toe.gamestate(board) == Ok(State.Ongoing)
    }
}

test "invalid boards" {
    cases = [
        #(
            "Invalid board: X went twice",
            ["XX ", "   ", "   "],
            "Wrong turn order: X went twice",
        ),
        #("Invalid board: O started", ["OOX", "   ", "   "], "Wrong turn order: O started"),
        #(
            "Invalid board: X won and O kept playing",
            ["XXX", "OOO", "   "],
            "Impossible board: game should have ended after the game was won",
        ),
        #(
            "Invalid board: players kept playing after a win",
            ["XXX", "OOO", "XOX"],
            "Impossible board: game should have ended after the game was won",
        ),
        #(
            "Invalid board: O kept playing after X wins",
            ["OO ", "XXX", " O "],
            "Impossible board: game should have ended after the game was won",
        ),
        #(
            "Invalid board: X kept playing after O wins",
            ["XX ", "OOO", " XX"],
            "Impossible board: game should have ended after the game was won",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, board, message), description {
        assert Err(error) = state_of_tic_tac_toe.gamestate(board)
        assert "${error}" == message
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- `gamestate` returns `Result<State, Error>`. `State` is the three canonical answers and `Error` the three ways a board breaks the rules; `Error`'s `Display` gives the canonical messages, so the variants carry no text.
- The board is read into one `Vector<Codepoint>` of nine cells, row by row, and the eight winning lines are a `once` list of position vectors. `has_won` is `Iter.any` over the lines of `Iter.all` over their cells.
- The rules are counts and wins: O never has more marks than X, X never more than one more than O, and the game stops at a win, so an X win leaves X one mark ahead and an O win leaves the counts equal. A win either way round, or both players winning, is the canonical "game should have ended" error.
- The checks run in the canonical order of precedence: turn order first, then play after a win, then the state. A board with every cell full and no line is a draw.
- The cases are four `subtests` tables by expected outcome. The invalid-board table asserts each error's message, which is what the canonical data gives. The two cases that newer ones reimplement (a middle-row win that broke the turn order, and an older error message) are left out.
